The conformance runner compares normalized HTML, so tag structure and\nentities must match the spec examples.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport string\nfrom collections.abc import Callable\n\nfrom mdparser.blocks import Block\n\nInlineParser = Callable[[str], str]\n\nESCAPES = ((\"&\", \"&amp;\"), (\"<\", \"&lt;\"), (\">\", \"&gt;\"), ('\"', \"&quot;\"))\nURL_SAFE_CHARS = frozenset(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + \";,/?:@&=+$-_.!~*'()#\")\nHEX_DIGITS = frozenset(string.hexdigits)\n\n\ndef escape_html(text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Escape &, <, > and \" so the text renders as literal characters. The ampersand goes first.\"\"\"\n    for raw, entity in ESCAPES:\n        text = text.replace(raw, entity)\n    return text\n\n\ndef percent_encode_url(url: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Percent-encode a URL for use in an attribute.\n\n    URL-safe ASCII and existing %XX escapes are kept. Every other character is encoded as its\n    UTF-8 bytes, so a lone % becomes %25.\n    \"\"\"\n    out: list[str] = []\n    index = 0\n    while index < len(url):\n        char = url[index]\n        if char == \"%\" and _is_hex_pair(url[index + 1 : index + 3]):\n            out.append(url[index : index + 3])\n            index += 3\n            continue\n        if char in URL_SAFE_CHARS:\n            out.append(char)\n        else:\n            out.extend(f\"%{byte:02X}\" for byte in char.encode(\"utf-8\"))\n        index += 1\n    return \"\".join(out)\n\n\ndef _is_hex_pair(text: str) -> bool:\n    return len(text) == 2 and all(char in HEX_DIGITS for char in text)\n\n\ndef render_document(root: Block, parse_inline: InlineParser) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Phase 2 walk: render the top-level blocks in order, one line ending after each block.\n\n    `parse_inline` is the inline parser hook. It receives the raw content of each paragraph and\n    returns that content's HTML.\n    \"\"\"\n    return \"\".join(_render_block(child, parse_inline) for child in root.children)\n\n\ndef _render_block(block: Block, parse_inline: InlineParser) -> str:\n    if block.kind.name == \"paragraph\":\n        return f\"<p>{parse_inline(block.content)}</p>\\n\"\n    if block.kind.name == \"thematic_break\":\n        return \"<hr />\\n\"\n    raise ValueError(f\"no HTML renderer for block type {block.kind.name!r}\")\n\"\"\"Process I/O boundary for the `commonmark` executable.\n\nResponsibility: read raw bytes from `sys.stdin.buffer`, decode UTF-8 with U+FFFD replacement,\nnormalize line endings, replace U+0000, and write HTML to `sys.stdout.buffer`. Diagnostics go to\n`sys.stderr` only, and the exit status is 0 for every input.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport re\nimport sys\n\nfrom mdparser import blocks, inlines, render\n\nREPLACEMENT_CHARACTER = \"�\"\nLINE_ENDING_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"\\r\\n|\\r|\\n\")\n\n\ndef decode_source(data: bytes) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Decode raw input bytes as UTF-8, replacing each invalid byte with U+FFFD.\"\"\"\n    return data.decode(\"utf-8\", errors=\"replace\")\n\n\ndef split_lines(text: str) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Split text on LF, CR, or CRLF, and replace each U+0000 with U+FFFD.\"\"\"\n    text = text.replace(\"\\x00\", REPLACEMENT_CHARACTER)\n    return LINE_ENDING_PATTERN.split(text)\n\n\ndef render_lines(lines: list[str]) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Parse the lines into a block tree and return the HTML document.\"\"\"\n    root = blocks.parse_lines(lines)\n    return render.render_document(root, lambda raw: inlines.parse_inline(raw, root.references))\n\n\ndef main() -> int:\n    \"\"\"Run the executable: stdin Markdown to stdout HTML. Always returns 0.\"\"\"\n    data = sys.stdin.buffer.read()\n    try:\n        lines = split_lines(decode_source(data))\n        html = render_lines(lines)\n    except Exception as exc:\n        print(f\"commonmark: internal error: {exc!r}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        html = \"\"\n    sys.stdout.buffer.write(html.encode(\"utf-8\"))\n    sys.stdout.buffer.flush()\n    return 0\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    sys.exit(main())\n\"\"\"Phase 2: inline parsing.\n\nResponsibility: parse the raw text of paragraphs and headings into inline nodes with the\ndelimiter-stack algorithms (look for link or image, process emphasis), using the reference map\nfrom `mdparser.refs`.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport re\nimport unicodedata\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field\n\nfrom mdparser.entities import ASCII_PUNCTUATION, match_reference\nfrom mdparser.links import LinkTail, match_inline_link, match_reference_tail\nfrom mdparser.refs import ReferenceMap\nfrom mdparser.render import escape_html, percent_encode_url\n\n# Inline nodes. A delimiter run is a `Text` node until emphasis consumes some of its characters;\n# whatever is left over is literal text. Everything else is already-rendered `Html`.\n# The bracket openers `[` and `![` are also `Text` nodes until a link or image closes over them.\nBRACKET_MARKERS = (\"[\", \"![\")\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Text:\n    \"\"\"An unconsumed run of `*` or `_` characters, escaped on output.\"\"\"\n\n    literal: str\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Html:\n    \"\"\"Rendered inline HTML: text, a code span, an autolink, raw HTML, or a decoded reference.\n\n    `text` is the node's plain-text value, used for image alt text: markup is dropped, and the\n    characters are unescaped.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    html: str\n    text: str\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Element:\n    \"\"\"An emphasis element. Its children are the nodes that sat between its opener and closer.\"\"\"\n\n    tag: str\n    children: list[\"Node\"] = field(default_factory=list)\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Link:\n    \"\"\"A link element. Its children are the nodes that sat between its brackets, already processed.\"\"\"\n\n    href: str\n    title: str | None\n    children: list[\"Node\"] = field(default_factory=list)\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Image:\n    \"\"\"An image. Its children are the nodes of its description, already processed; they give the alt text.\"\"\"\n\n    destination: str\n    title: str | None\n    children: list[\"Node\"] = field(default_factory=list)\n\n\nNode = Text | Html | Element | Link | Image\n\n\n@dataclass(eq=False)\nclass Delimiter:\n    \"\"\"A delimiter stack entry. The rest act on the\nblock tree returned by `parse_lines` and on the exact stdout bytes, which is the state handed back.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport subprocess\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom mdparser.blocks import PARAGRAPH, THEMATIC_BREAK, parse_lines\n\n\ndef run_commonmark(project_root: Path, source: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:\n    return subprocess.run(\n        [str(project_root / \"commonmark\")],\n        input=source,\n        capture_output=True,\n        text=True,\n        cwd=project_root,\n        check=False,\n    )\n\n\ndef kinds(lines: list[str]) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Names of the top-level block types that `lines` produce, in order.\"\"\"\n    return [child.kind.name for child in parse_lines(lines).children]\n\n\n# --- Declared acceptance checks (transcribed from FEATURE-Thematic-Breaks.md) ---\n\n\ndef test_thematic_three_markers(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Lines of three or more matching marker characters each render one hr element.\"\"\"\n    lines = [\"***\", \"---\", \"___\", \"_____________\", \" - - -\", \" **  * ** * ** * **\"]\n    source = \"\\n\\n\".join(lines) + \"\\n\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, source)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<hr />\") == len(lines)\n\n\ndef test_thematic_not_a_break(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Wrong characters, too few characters, mixed characters and trailing text do not produce hr elements.\"\"\"\n    source = \"+++\\n\\n--\\n\\n_ _ _ _ a\\n\\na------\\n\\n *-*\\n\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, source)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<hr />\") == 0\n\n\ndef test_thematic_interrupts_paragraph(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A thematic break directly after paragraph text splits it into two paragraphs around one hr.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"Foo\\n***\\nbar\\n\")\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<hr />\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 2\n\n\ndef test_thematic_trailing_whitespace(project_root: Path) -> None:\n\"\"\"Shared pytest fixtures for the mdparser test suite.\"\"\"\n\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport pytest\n\nPROJECT_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef project_root() -> Path:\n    \"\"\"Absolute path to the application root, where `commonmark` and `pyproject.toml` live.\"\"\"\n    return PROJECT_ROOT\n\"\"\"Block engine tests: column helpers, the cursor, the registry, and the per-line procedure.\n\nEach test builds a block tree with `parse_lines` and reads back the tree: child block type names,\nparagraph content, and raw lines. The ampersand goes first.\"\"\"\n    for raw, entity in ESCAPES:\n        text = text.replace(raw, entity)\n    return text\n\n\ndef percent_encode_url(url: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Percent-encode a URL for use in an attribute.\n\n    URL-safe ASCII and existing %XX escapes are kept. Every other character is encoded as its\n    UTF-8 bytes, so a lone % becomes %25.\n    \"\"\"\n    out: list[str] = []\n    index = 0\n    while index < len(url):\n        char = url[index]\n        if char == \"%\" and _is_hex_pair(url[index + 1 : index + 3]):\n            out.append(url[index : index + 3])\n            index += 3\n            continue\n        if char in URL_SAFE_CHARS:\n            out.append(char)\n        else:\n            out.extend(f\"%{byte:02X}\" for byte in char.encode(\"utf-8\"))\n        index += 1\n    return \"\".join(out)\n\n\ndef _is_hex_pair(text: str) -> bool:\n    return len(text) == 2 and all(char in HEX_DIGITS for char in text)\n\n\ndef render_document(root: Block, parse_inline: InlineParser) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Phase 2 walk: render the top-level blocks in order, one line ending after each block.\n\n    `parse_inline` is the inline parser hook. It receives the raw content of each paragraph and\n    returns that content's HTML.\n    \"\"\"\n    return \"\".join(_render_block(child, parse_inline) for child in root.children)\n\n\ndef _render_block(block: Block, parse_inline: InlineParser) -> str:\n    if block.kind.name == \"paragraph\":\n        return f\"<p>{parse_inline(block.content)}</p>\\n\"\n    if block.kind.name == \"thematic_break\":\n        return \"<hr />\\n\"\n    raise ValueError(f\"no HTML renderer for block type {block.kind.name!r}\")\n\"\"\"Process I/O boundary for the `commonmark` executable.\n\nResponsibility: read raw bytes from `sys.stdin.buffer`, decode UTF-8 with U+FFFD replacement,\nnormalize line endings, replace U+0000, and write HTML to `sys.stdout.buffer`. Diagnostics go to\n`sys.stderr` only, and the exit status is 0 for every input.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport re\nimport sys\n\nfrom mdparser import blocks, inlines, render\n\nREPLACEMENT_CHARACTER = \"�\"\nLINE_ENDING_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"\\r\\n|\\r|\\n\")\n\n\ndef decode_source(data: bytes) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Decode raw input bytes as UTF-8, replacing each invalid byte with U+FFFD.\"\"\"\n    return data.decode(\"utf-8\", errors=\"replace\")\n\n\ndef split_lines(text: str) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Split text on LF, CR, or CRLF, and replace each U+0000 with U+FFFD.\"\"\"\n    text = text.replace(\"\\x00\", REPLACEMENT_CHARACTER)\n    return LINE_ENDING_PATTERN.split(text)\n\n\ndef render_lines(lines: list[str]) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Parse the lines into a block tree and return the HTML document.\"\"\"\n    root = blocks.parse_lines(lines)\n    return render.render_document(root, lambda raw: inlines.parse_inline(raw, root.references))\n\n\ndef main() -> int:\n    \"\"\"Run the executable: stdin Markdown to stdout HTML. Always returns 0.\"\"\"\n    data = sys.stdin.buffer.read()\n    try:\n        lines = split_lines(decode_source(data))\n        html = render_lines(lines)\n    except Exception as exc:\n        print(f\"commonmark: internal error: {exc!r}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        html = \"\"\n    sys.stdout.buffer.write(html.encode(\"utf-8\"))\n    sys.stdout.buffer.flush()\n    return 0\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    sys.exit(main())\n\"\"\"Phase 2: inline parsing.\n\nResponsibility: parse the raw text of paragraphs and headings into inline nodes with the\ndelimiter-stack algorithms (look for link or image, process emphasis), using the reference map\nfrom `mdparser.refs`.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport re\nimport unicodedata\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field\n\nfrom mdparser.entities import ASCII_PUNCTUATION, match_reference\nfrom mdparser.links import LinkTail, match_inline_link, match_reference_tail\nfrom mdparser.refs import ReferenceMap\nfrom mdparser.render import escape_html, percent_encode_url\n\n# Inline nodes. A delimiter run is a `Text` node until emphasis consumes some of its characters;\n# whatever is left over is literal text. Everything else is already-rendered `Html`.\n# The bracket openers `[` and `![` are also `Text` nodes until a link or image closes over them.\nBRACKET_MARKERS = (\"[\", \"![\")\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Text:\n    \"\"\"An unconsumed run of `*` or `_` characters, escaped on output.\"\"\"\n\n    literal: str\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Html:\n    \"\"\"Rendered inline HTML: text, a code span, an autolink, raw HTML, or a decoded reference.\n\n    `text` is the node's plain-text value, used for image alt text: markup is dropped, and the\n    characters are unescaped.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    html: str\n    text: str\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Element:\n    \"\"\"An emphasis element. Its children are the nodes that sat between its opener and closer.\"\"\"\n\n    tag: str\n    children: list[\"Node\"] = field(default_factory=list)\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Link:\n    \"\"\"A link element. Its children are the nodes that sat between its brackets, already processed.\"\"\"\n\n    href: str\n    title: str | None\n    children: list[\"Node\"] = field(default_factory=list)\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Image:\n    \"\"\"An image. Zero for every other block.\n        self.level = 0\n        # The document-wide reference map. Only the document root holds one.","originalFile":"\"\"\"Phase 1: block tree, block-type registry, per-line procedure, and lazy continuation.\n\nResponsibility: consume lines one at a time, match them against open blocks, look for new block\nstarts, and add remaining text to the deepest open block. Link reference definitions are handed to\n`mdparser.refs` when a paragraph closes.\n\nEach block type is a `BlockType` record registered in a `BlockRegistry`. A type supplies a start\nrule, a continue rule and a close (finalize) rule; the per-line loop in `DocumentParser` never\nnames a concrete type.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom collections.abc import Callable, Iterable\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\nfrom mdparser.refs import ReferenceMap, extract_definitions\n\nTAB_STOP = 4\nSPACE_CHARS = \" \\t\"\n\n# A start rule inspects the rest of the line below `container`. It returns a new block, after\n# advancing the cursor past its marker, or None, leaving the cursor untouched.\nStartRule = Callable[[\"Cursor\", \"Block\"], \"Block | None\"]\n# A continue rule decides whether the line continues an open block. It advances the cursor only\n# when it returns True.\nContinueRule = Callable[[\"Block\", \"Cursor\"], bool]\n# An add-line rule appends the remaining line text to a leaf block that accepts lines.\nAddLineRule = Callable[[\"Block\", \"Cursor\"], None]\n# A finalize rule runs once when a block closes, for example to set its content.\nFinalizeRule = Callable[[\"Block\"], None]\n\n\ndef next_column(char: str, col: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the column after `char`, which sits at column `col`. Tabs advance to the next tab stop.\"\"\"\n    if char == \"\\t\":\n        return col + TAB_STOP - col % TAB_STOP\n    return col + 1\n\n\ndef indent_columns(line: str, pos: int, col: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the width in columns of the spaces and tabs starting at `pos`, which sits at `col`.\"\"\"\n    end = pos\n    end_col = col\n    while end < len(line) and line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:\n        end_col = next_column(line[end], end_col)\n        end += 1\n    return end_col - col\n\n\nclass Cursor:\n    \"\"\"A position in one source line, tracked both as a character index and as a column.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, line: str) -> None:\n        self.line = line\n        self.pos = 0\n        self.col = 0\n\n    @property\n    def rest(self) -> str:\n        \"\"\"The text from the current position to the end of the line.\"\"\"\n        return self.line[self.pos :]\n\n    @property\n    def indent(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Columns of indentation from the current position to the next non-space character.\"\"\"\n        return indent_columns(self.line, self.pos, self.col)\n\n    def next_nonspace(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Index of the first character at or after the current position that is not a space or tab.\"\"\"\n        end = self.pos\n        while end < len(self.line) and self.line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            end += 1\n        return end\n\n    def is_blank(self) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"True when only spaces and tabs remain on the line.\"\"\"\n        return self.next_nonspace() == len(self.line)\n\n    def advance_to(self, index: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Move the cursor forward to character `index`, tracking the column.\"\"\"\n        while self.pos < index:\n            self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n            self.pos += 1\n\n    def advance_nonspace(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Skip spaces and tabs up to the next non-space character.\"\"\"\n        self.advance_to(self.next_nonspace())\n\n    def advance_columns(self, columns: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Consume spaces and tabs until `columns` columns are passed.\n\n        A tab that straddles the target column is consumed whole, so the column may overshoot.\n        \"\"\"\n        target = self.col + columns\n        while self.pos < len(self.line) and self.col < target and self.line[self.pos] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n            self.pos += 1\n\n\nclass Block:\n    \"\"\"A node in the block tree. Leaf blocks keep their raw lines; `content` is set when they close.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, kind: BlockType) -> None:\n        self.kind = kind\n        self.parent: Block | None = None\n        self.children: list[Block] = []\n        self.is_open = True\n        self.lines: list[str] = []\n        self.content = \"\"\n        # The document-wide reference map. Only the document root holds one.\n        self.references: ReferenceMap | None = None\n\n    def open_last_child(self) -> Block | None:\n        \"\"\"The last child if it is still open, otherwise None.\"\"\"\n        if self.children and self.children[-1].is_open:\n            return self.children[-1]\n        return None\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass BlockType:\n    \"\"\"The rules that define one kind of block.\n\n    `accepts_lines` marks a leaf that takes line text. `interruptible` lets a start rule close such\n    a leaf (a paragraph); a non-interruptible leaf blocks new starts. `lazy` lets a non-matching\n    line join this block as a lazy continuation. `is_container` lets the block hold child blocks.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    name: str\n    continues: ContinueRule\n    is_container: bool = False\n    accepts_lines: bool = False\n    interruptible: bool = False\n    lazy: bool = False\n    start: StartRule | None = None\n    add_line: AddLineRule | None = None\n    finalize: FinalizeRule | None = None\n\n    def __post_init__(self) -> None:\n        if self.accepts_lines and self.add_line is None:\n            raise ValueError(f\"block type {self.name!r} accepts lines but has no add_line rule\")\n        if self.lazy and not self.accepts_lines:\n            raise ValueError(f\"block type {self.name!r} is lazy but does not accept lines\")\n\n\ndef _always_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    return True\n\n\ndef _paragraph_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    return not cursor.is_blank()\n\n\ndef _paragraph_add_line(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:\n    cursor.advance_nonspace()\n    block.lines.append(cursor.rest)\n\n\ndef _paragraph_finalize(block: Block) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Move leading link reference definitions into the document map and keep the remaining text.\n\n    A paragraph that holds only definitions leaves the tree.\n    \"\"\"\n    text = \"\\n\".join(block.lines).strip(\" \\t\")\n    block.content = extract_definitions(text, _document_references(block))\n    if not block.content and block.parent is not None:\n        block.parent.children.remove(block)\n\n\ndef _document_references(block: Block) -> ReferenceMap:\n    \"\"\"The reference map of the document root that `block` belongs to.\"\"\"\n    root = block\n    while root.parent is not None:\n        root = root.parent\n    assert root.references is not None\n    return root.references\n\n\ndef _never_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    return False\n\n\nTHEMATIC_BREAK_MARKERS = \"*-_\"\nTHEMATIC_BREAK_MIN_MARKERS = 3\n\n\ndef _thematic_break_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    \"\"\"Start a thematic break when the rest of the line is three or more matching marker characters.\n\n    Spaces and tabs may appear between and after the markers. Any other character, or four or more\n    columns of indentation, means the line is not a thematic break.\n    \"\"\"\n    if cursor.indent >= 4:\n        return None\n    start = cursor.next_nonspace()\n    line = cursor.line\n    if start == len(line) or line[start] not in THEMATIC_BREAK_MARKERS:\n        return None\n    marker = line[start]\n    count = 0\n    for char in line[start:]:\n        if char == marker:\n            count += 1\n        elif char not in SPACE_CHARS:\n            return None\n    if count < THEMATIC_BREAK_MIN_MARKERS:\n        return None\n    cursor.advance_to(len(line))\n    return Block(THEMATIC_BREAK)\n\n\nDOCUMENT = BlockType(\"document\", continues=_always_continues, is_container=True)\nPARAGRAPH = BlockType(\n    \"paragraph\",\n    continues=_paragraph_continues,\n    accepts_lines=True,\n    interruptible=True,\n    lazy=True,\n    add_line=_paragraph_add_line,\n    finalize=_paragraph_finalize,\n)\n# A thematic break is a complete single-line block. It never takes continuation lines, so it closes\n# as soon as the next line arrives.\nTHEMATIC_BREAK = BlockType(\n    \"thematic_break\",\n    continues=_never_continues,\n    start=_thematic_break_start,\n)\n\n\nclass BlockRegistry:\n    \"\"\"The block types a parse may use: the document root, the fallback paragraph, and start rules.\n\n    Start rules are tried in registration order. The fallback type is the paragraph created when no\n    start rule matches a line of text.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, root: BlockType, fallback: BlockType) -> None:\n        self.root = root\n        self.fallback = fallback\n        self._names: set[str] = set()\n        self._starts: list[BlockType] = []\n        self.register(root)\n        self.register(fallback)\n\n    def register(self, block_type: BlockType) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Add a block type. Its start rule, if any, joins the start rules in order.\"\"\"\n        if block_type.name in self._names:\n            raise ValueError(f\"block type already registered: {block_type.name!r}\")\n        self._names.add(block_type.name)\n        if block_type.start is not None:\n            self._starts.append(block_type)\n\n    def starts(self) -> tuple[BlockType, ...]:\n        \"\"\"The registered block types that have a start rule, in registration order.\"\"\"\n        return tuple(self._starts)\n\n\nDEFAULT_REGISTRY = BlockRegistry(root=DOCUMENT, fallback=PARAGRAPH)\nDEFAULT_REGISTRY.register(THEMATIC_BREAK)\n\n\nclass DocumentParser:\n    \"\"\"Runs the phase 1 per-line procedure over a document, one line at a time.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, registry: BlockRegistry = DEFAULT_REGISTRY) -> None:\n        self.registry = registry\n        self.root = Block(registry.root)\n        self.root.references = ReferenceMap()\n\n    def incorporate_line(self, line: str) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Match open blocks, look for new starts, then add the remaining text.\"\"\"\n        cursor = Cursor(line)\n\n        # 1. Match open blocks. Unmatched blocks stay open: the line may be a lazy continuation.\n        container = self._match_open_blocks(cursor)\n        all_closed = container.open_last_child() is None\n\n        # 2. Look for new block starts. Unmatched blocks are closed only once a start succeeds.\n        started = False\n        while not self._is_text_leaf(container):\n            new_block = self._try_starts(cursor, container)\n            if new_block is None:\n                break\n            if not started:\n                started = True\n                all_closed = True\n                self._close_below(container)\n            self._attach(new_block, container)\n            container = new_block\n\n        # 3. Add the remaining text to the deepest open block.\n        tip = self._tip()\n        if not all_closed and not cursor.is_blank() and tip.kind.lazy:\n            self._add_line(tip, cursor)\n            return\n        self._close_below(container)\n        if container.kind.accepts_lines:\n            self._add_line(container, cursor)\n        elif not cursor.is_blank():\n            paragraph = Block(self.registry.fallback)\n            self._attach(paragraph, container)\n            self._add_line(paragraph, cursor)\n\n    def finish(self) -> Block:\n        \"\"\"Close every open block and return the document root.\"\"\"\n        self._close_below(self.root)\n        self.root.is_open = False\n        return self.root\n\n    def _match_open_blocks(self, cursor: Cursor) -> Block:\n        container = self.root\n        while True:\n            child = container.open_last_child()\n            if child is None or not child.kind.continues(child, cursor):\n                return container\n            container = child\n\n    def _try_starts(self, cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n        for block_type in self.registry.starts():\n            assert block_type.start is not None\n            new_block = block_type.start(cursor, container)\n            if new_block is not None:\n                return new_block\n        return None\n\n    def _is_text_leaf(self, block: Block) -> bool:\n        return block.kind.accepts_lines and not block.kind.interruptible\n\n    def _attach(self, new_block: Block, container: Block) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Add `new_block` under `container`, closing any leaf that cannot hold it.\"\"\"\n        while not container.kind.is_container:\n            self._finalize(container)\n            assert container.parent is not None\n            container = container.parent\n        container.children.append(new_block)\n        new_block.parent = container\n\n    def _add_line(self, block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:\n        assert block.kind.add_line is not None\n        block.kind.add_line(block, cursor)\n\n    def _tip(self) -> Block:\n        \"\"\"The deepest open block.\"\"\"\n        tip = self.root\n        while (child := tip.open_last_child()) is not None:\n            tip = child\n        return tip\n\n    def _close_below(self, container: Block) -> None:\n        child = container.open_last_child()\n        if child is None:\n            return\n        self._close_below(child)\n        self._finalize(child)\n\n    def _finalize(self, block: Block) -> None:\n        block.is_open = False\n        if block.kind.finalize is not None:\n            block.kind.finalize(block)\n\n\ndef parse_lines(lines: Iterable[str], registry: BlockRegistry = DEFAULT_REGISTRY) -> Block:\n    \"\"\"Build the block tree for `lines`, which hold no line-ending characters.\"\"\"\n    parser = DocumentParser(registry)\n    for line in lines:\n        parser.incorporate_line(line)\n    return parser.finish()\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":108,"oldLines":6,"newStart":108,"newLines":8,"lines":["         self.is_open = True","         self.lines: list[str] = []"," So `foo#` keeps its hash, and so\n    does `foo \\\\#`, where the backslash is not whitespace.\n    \"\"\"\n    stripped = content.rstrip(ATX_MARKER)\n    if stripped == content:\n        return content\n    if stripped == \"\" or stripped[-1] in SPACE_CHARS:\n        return stripped.rstrip(SPACE_CHARS)\n    return content\n\n\nDOCUMENT","originalFile":"\"\"\"Phase 1: block tree, block-type registry, per-line procedure, and lazy continuation.\n\nResponsibility: consume lines one at a time, match them against open blocks, look for new block\nstarts, and add remaining text to the deepest open block. Link reference definitions are handed to\n`mdparser.refs` when a paragraph closes.\n\nEach block type is a `BlockType` record registered in a `BlockRegistry`. A type supplies a start\nrule, a continue rule and a close (finalize) rule; the per-line loop in `DocumentParser` never\nnames a concrete type.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom collections.abc import Callable, Iterable\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\nfrom mdparser.refs import ReferenceMap, extract_definitions\n\nTAB_STOP = 4\nSPACE_CHARS = \" \\t\"\n\n# A start rule inspects the rest of the line below `container`. It returns a new block, after\n# advancing the cursor past its marker, or None, leaving the cursor untouched.\nStartRule = Callable[[\"Cursor\", \"Block\"], \"Block | None\"]\n# A continue rule decides whether the line continues an open block. It advances the cursor only\n# when it returns True.\nContinueRule = Callable[[\"Block\", \"Cursor\"], bool]\n# An add-line rule appends the remaining line text to a leaf block that accepts lines.\nAddLineRule = Callable[[\"Block\", \"Cursor\"], None]\n# A finalize rule runs once when a block closes, for example to set its content.\nFinalizeRule = Callable[[\"Block\"], None]\n\n\ndef next_column(char: str, col: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the column after `char`, which sits at column `col`. Tabs advance to the next tab stop.\"\"\"\n    if char == \"\\t\":\n        return col + TAB_STOP - col % TAB_STOP\n    return col + 1\n\n\ndef indent_columns(line: str, pos: int, col: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the width in columns of the spaces and tabs starting at `pos`, which sits at `col`.\"\"\"\n    end = pos\n    end_col = col\n    while end < len(line) and line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:\n        end_col = next_column(line[end], end_col)\n        end += 1\n    return end_col - col\n\n\nclass Cursor:\n    \"\"\"A position in one source line, tracked both as a character index and as a column.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, line: str) -> None:\n        self.line = line\n        self.pos = 0\n        self.col = 0\n\n    @property\n    def rest(self) -> str:\n        \"\"\"The text from the current position to the end of the line.\"\"\"\n        return self.line[self.pos :]\n\n    @property\n    def indent(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Columns of indentation from the current position to the next non-space character.\"\"\"\n        return indent_columns(self.line, self.pos, self.col)\n\n    def next_nonspace(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Index of the first character at or after the current position that is not a space or tab.\"\"\"\n        end = self.pos\n        while end < len(self.line) and self.line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            end += 1\n        return end\n\n    def is_blank(self) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"True when only spaces and tabs remain on the line.\"\"\"\n        return self.next_nonspace() == len(self.line)\n\n    def advance_to(self, index: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Move the cursor forward to character `index`, tracking the column.\"\"\"\n        while self.pos < index:\n            self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n            self.pos += 1\n\n    def advance_nonspace(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Skip spaces and tabs up to the next non-space character.\"\"\"\n        self.advance_to(self.next_nonspace())\n\n    def advance_columns(self, columns: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Consume spaces and tabs until `columns` columns are passed.\n\n        A tab that straddles the target column is consumed whole, so the column may overshoot.\n        \"\"\"\n        target = self.col + columns\n        while self.pos < len(self.line) and self.col < target and self.line[self.pos] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n            self.pos += 1\n\n\nclass Block:\n    \"\"\"A node in the block tree. Leaf blocks keep their raw lines; `content` is set when they close.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, kind: BlockType) -> None:\n        self.kind = kind\n        self.parent: Block | None = None\n        self.children: list[Block] = []\n        self.is_open = True\n        self.lines: list[str] = []\n        self.content = \"\"\n        # Heading level, 1 to 6, for an ATX heading. Zero for every other block.\n        self.level = 0\n        # The document-wide reference map. Only the document root holds one.\n        self.references: ReferenceMap | None = None\n\n    def open_last_child(self) -> Block | None:\n        \"\"\"The last child if it is still open, otherwise None.\"\"\"\n        if self.children and self.children[-1].is_open:\n            return self.children[-1]\n        return None\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass BlockType:\n    \"\"\"The rules that define one kind of block.\n\n    `accepts_lines` marks a leaf that takes line text. `interruptible` lets a start rule close such\n    a leaf (a paragraph); a non-interruptible leaf blocks new starts. `lazy` lets a non-matching\n    line join this block as a lazy continuation. `is_container` lets the block hold child blocks.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    name: str\n    continues: ContinueRule\n    is_container: bool = False\n    accepts_lines: bool = False\n    interruptible: bool = False\n    lazy: bool = False\n    start: StartRule | None = None\n    add_line: AddLineRule | None = None\n    finalize: FinalizeRule | None = None\n\n    def __post_init__(self) -> None:\n        if self.accepts_lines and self.add_line is None:\n            raise ValueError(f\"block type {self.name!r} accepts lines but has no add_line rule\")\n        if self.lazy and not self.accepts_lines:\n            raise ValueError(f\"block type {self.name!r} is lazy but does not accept lines\")\n\n\ndef _always_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    return True\n\n\ndef _paragraph_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    return not cursor.is_blank()\n\n\ndef _paragraph_add_line(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:\n    cursor.advance_nonspace()\n    block.lines.append(cursor.rest)\n\n\ndef _paragraph_finalize(block: Block) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Move leading link reference definitions into the document map and keep the remaining text.\n\n    A paragraph that holds only definitions leaves the tree.\n    \"\"\"\n    text = \"\\n\".join(block.lines).strip(\" \\t\")\n    block.content = extract_definitions(text, _document_references(block))\n    if not block.content and block.parent is not None:\n        block.parent.children.remove(block)\n\n\ndef _document_references(block: Block) -> ReferenceMap:\n    \"\"\"The reference map of the document root that `block` belongs to.\"\"\"\n    root = block\n    while root.parent is not None:\n        root = root.parent\n    assert root.references is not None\n    return root.references\n\n\ndef _never_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    return False\n\n\nTHEMATIC_BREAK_MARKERS = \"*-_\"\nTHEMATIC_BREAK_MIN_MARKERS = 3\n\n\ndef _thematic_break_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    \"\"\"Start a thematic break when the rest of the line is three or more matching marker characters.\n\n    Spaces and tabs may appear between and after the markers. Any other character, or four or more\n    columns of indentation, means the line is not a thematic break.\n    \"\"\"\n    if cursor.indent >= 4:\n        return None\n    start = cursor.next_nonspace()\n    line = cursor.line\n    if start == len(line) or line[start] not in THEMATIC_BREAK_MARKERS:\n        return None\n    marker = line[start]\n    count = 0\n    for char in line[start:]:\n        if char == marker:\n            count += 1\n        elif char not in SPACE_CHARS:\n            return None\n    if count < THEMATIC_BREAK_MIN_MARKERS:\n        return None\n    cursor.advance_to(len(line))\n    return Block(THEMATIC_BREAK)\n\n\nDOCUMENT = BlockType(\"document\", continues=_always_continues, is_container=True)\nPARAGRAPH = BlockType(\n    \"paragraph\",\n    continues=_paragraph_continues,\n    accepts_lines=True,\n    interruptible=True,\n    lazy=True,\n    add_line=_paragraph_add_line,\n    finalize=_paragraph_finalize,\n)\n# A thematic break is a complete single-line block. It never takes continuation lines, so it closes\n# as soon as the next line arrives.\nTHEMATIC_BREAK = BlockType(\n    \"thematic_break\",\n    continues=_never_continues,\n    start=_thematic_break_start,\n)\n\n\nclass BlockRegistry:\n    \"\"\"The block types a parse may use: the document root, the fallback paragraph, and start rules.\n\n    Start rules are tried in registration order. The fallback type is the paragraph created when no\n    start rule matches a line of text.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, root: BlockType, fallback: BlockType) -> None:\n        self.root = root\n        self.fallback = fallback\n        self._names: set[str] = set()\n        self._starts: list[BlockType] = []\n        self.register(root)\n        self.register(fallback)\n\n    def register(self, block_type: BlockType) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Add a block type. Its start rule, if any, joins the start rules in order.\"\"\"\n        if block_type.name in self._names:\n            raise ValueError(f\"block type already registered: {block_type.name!r}\")\n        self._names.add(block_type.name)\n        if block_type.start is not None:\n            self._starts.append(block_type)\n\n    def starts(self) -> tuple[BlockType, ...]:\n        \"\"\"The registered block types that have a start rule, in registration order.\"\"\"\n        return tuple(self._starts)\n\n\nDEFAULT_REGISTRY = BlockRegistry(root=DOCUMENT, fallback=PARAGRAPH)\nDEFAULT_REGISTRY.register(THEMATIC_BREAK)\n\n\nclass DocumentParser:\n    \"\"\"Runs the phase 1 per-line procedure over a document, one line at a time.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, registry: BlockRegistry = DEFAULT_REGISTRY) -> None:\n        self.registry = registry\n        self.root = Block(registry.root)\n        self.root.references = ReferenceMap()\n\n    def incorporate_line(self, line: str) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Match open blocks, look for new starts, then add the remaining text.\"\"\"\n        cursor = Cursor(line)\n\n        # 1. Match open blocks. Unmatched blocks stay open: the line may be a lazy continuation.\n        container = self._match_open_blocks(cursor)\n        all_closed = container.open_last_child() is None\n\n        # 2. Look for new block starts. Unmatched blocks are closed only once a start succeeds.\n        started = False\n        while not self._is_text_leaf(container):\n            new_block = self._try_starts(cursor, container)\n            if new_block is None:\n                break\n            if not started:\n                started = True\n                all_closed = True\n                self._close_below(container)\n            self._attach(new_block, container)\n            container = new_block\n\n        # 3. Add the remaining text to the deepest open block.\n        tip = self._tip()\n        if not all_closed and not cursor.is_blank() and tip.kind.lazy:\n            self._add_line(tip, cursor)\n            return\n        self._close_below(container)\n        if container.kind.accepts_lines:\n            self._add_line(container, cursor)\n        elif not cursor.is_blank():\n            paragraph = Block(self.registry.fallback)\n            self._attach(paragraph, container)\n            self._add_line(paragraph, cursor)\n\n    def finish(self) -> Block:\n        \"\"\"Close every open block and return the document root.\"\"\"\n        self._close_below(self.root)\n        self.root.is_open = False\n        return self.root\n\n    def _match_open_blocks(self, cursor: Cursor) -> Block:\n        container = self.root\n        while True:\n            child = container.open_last_child()\n            if child is None or not child.kind.continues(child, cursor):\n                return container\n            container = child\n\n    def _try_starts(self, cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n        for block_type in self.registry.starts():\n            assert block_type.start is not None\n            new_block = block_type.start(cursor, container)\n            if new_block is not None:\n                return new_block\n        return None\n\n    def _is_text_leaf(self, block: Block) -> bool:\n        return block.kind.accepts_lines and not block.kind.interruptible\n\n    def _attach(self, new_block: Block, container: Block) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Add `new_block` under `container`, closing any leaf that cannot hold it.\"\"\"\n        while not container.kind.is_container:\n            self._finalize(container)\n            assert container.parent is not None\n            container = container.parent\n        container.children.append(new_block)\n        new_block.parent = container\n\n    def _add_line(self, block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:\n        assert block.kind.add_line is not None\n        block.kind.add_line(block, cursor)\n\n    def _tip(self) -> Block:\n        \"\"\"The deepest open block.\"\"\"\n        tip = self.root\n        while (child := tip.open_last_child()) is not None:\n            tip = child\n        return tip\n\n    def _close_below(self, container: Block) -> None:\n        child = container.open_last_child()\n        if child is None:\n            return\n        self._close_below(child)\n        self._finalize(child)\n\n    def _finalize(self, block: Block) -> None:\n        block.is_open = False\n        if block.kind.finalize is not None:\n            block.kind.finalize(block)\n\n\ndef parse_lines(lines: Iterable[str], registry: BlockRegistry = DEFAULT_REGISTRY) -> The content is the","+    rest of the line, stripped of surrounding spaces and tabs, without a closing sequence.","+    \"\"\"","+    if cursor.indent >= 4:","+        return None","+    line = cursor.line","+    start = cursor.next_nonspace()","+    end = start","+    while end < len(line) and line[end] == ATX_MARKER:","+        end += 1","+    level = end - start","+    if not 1 <= level <= ATX_MAX_LEVEL:","+        return None","+    if end < len(line) and line[end] not in SPACE_CHARS:","+        return None","+    cursor.advance_to(len(line))","+    heading = Block(ATX_HEADING)","+    heading.level = level","+    heading.content = _strip_closing_sequence(line[end:].strip(SPACE_CHARS))","+    return heading","+","+","+def _strip_closing_sequence(content: str) -> str:","+    \"\"\"Remove a closing run of `#` characters from the end of heading content.","+","+    The run must be the whole content or follow a space or tab. So `foo#` keeps its hash, and so","+    does `foo \\\\#`, where the backslash is not whitespace.","+    \"\"\"","+    stripped = content.rstrip(ATX_MARKER)","+    if stripped == content:","+        return content","+    if stripped == \"\" or stripped[-1] in SPACE_CHARS:","+        return stripped.rstrip(SPACE_CHARS)","+    return content","+","+"," DOCUMENT = BlockType(\"document\", continues=_always_continues, is_container=True)"," PARAGRAPH = BlockType(","     \"paragraph\","]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false,"contentNotInModelContext":true},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01GR1wLj9xRgHpipMAdURTFM","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

Its content is parsed as\n# inlines when the document is rendered.\nATX_HEADING = BlockType(\n    \"atx_heading\",\n    continues=_never_continues,\n    start=_atx_heading_start,\n)\n","originalFile":"\"\"\"Phase 1: block tree, block-type registry, per-line procedure, and lazy continuation.\n\nResponsibility: consume lines one at a time, match them against open blocks, look for new block\nstarts, and add remaining text to the deepest open block. Link reference definitions are handed to\n`mdparser.refs` when a paragraph closes.\n\nEach block type is a `BlockType` record registered in a `BlockRegistry`. A type supplies a start\nrule, a continue rule and a close (finalize) rule; the per-line loop in `DocumentParser` never\nnames a concrete type.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom collections.abc import Callable, Iterable\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\nfrom mdparser.refs import ReferenceMap, extract_definitions\n\nTAB_STOP = 4\nSPACE_CHARS = \" \\t\"\n\n# A start rule inspects the rest of the line below `container`. It returns a new block, after\n# advancing the cursor past its marker, or None, leaving the cursor untouched.\nStartRule = Callable[[\"Cursor\", \"Block\"], \"Block | None\"]\n# A continue rule decides whether the line continues an open block. It advances the cursor only\n# when it returns True.\nContinueRule = Callable[[\"Block\", \"Cursor\"], bool]\n# An add-line rule appends the remaining line text to a leaf block that accepts lines.\nAddLineRule = Callable[[\"Block\", \"Cursor\"], None]\n# A finalize rule runs once when a block closes, for example to set its content.\nFinalizeRule = Callable[[\"Block\"], None]\n\n\ndef next_column(char: str, col: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the column after `char`, which sits at column `col`. Tabs advance to the next tab stop.\"\"\"\n    if char == \"\\t\":\n        return col + TAB_STOP - col % TAB_STOP\n    return col + 1\n\n\ndef indent_columns(line: str, pos: int, col: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the width in columns of the spaces and tabs starting at `pos`, which sits at `col`.\"\"\"\n    end = pos\n    end_col = col\n    while end < len(line) and line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:\n        end_col = next_column(line[end], end_col)\n        end += 1\n    return end_col - col\n\n\nclass Cursor:\n    \"\"\"A position in one source line, tracked both as a character index and as a column.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, line: str) -> None:\n        self.line = line\n        self.pos = 0\n        self.col = 0\n\n    @property\n    def rest(self) -> str:\n        \"\"\"The text from the current position to the end of the line.\"\"\"\n        return self.line[self.pos :]\n\n    @property\n    def indent(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Columns of indentation from the current position to the next non-space character.\"\"\"\n        return indent_columns(self.line, self.pos, self.col)\n\n    def next_nonspace(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Index of the first character at or after the current position that is not a space or tab.\"\"\"\n        end = self.pos\n        while end < len(self.line) and self.line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            end += 1\n        return end\n\n    def is_blank(self) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"True when only spaces and tabs remain on the line.\"\"\"\n        return self.next_nonspace() == len(self.line)\n\n    def advance_to(self, index: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Move the cursor forward to character `index`, tracking the column.\"\"\"\n        while self.pos < index:\n            self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n            self.pos += 1\n\n    def advance_nonspace(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Skip spaces and tabs up to the next non-space character.\"\"\"\n        self.advance_to(self.next_nonspace())\n\n    def advance_columns(self, columns: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Consume spaces and tabs until `columns` columns are passed.\n\n        A tab that straddles the target column is consumed whole, so the column may overshoot.\n        \"\"\"\n        target = self.col + columns\n        while self.pos < len(self.line) and self.col < target and self.line[self.pos] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n            self.pos += 1\n\n\nclass Block:\n    \"\"\"A node in the block tree. Leaf blocks keep their raw lines; `content` is set when they close.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, kind: BlockType) -> None:\n        self.kind = kind\n        self.parent: Block | None = None\n        self.children: list[Block] = []\n        self.is_open = True\n        self.lines: list[str] = []\n        self.content = \"\"\n        # Heading level, 1 to 6, for an ATX heading. Zero for every other block.\n        self.level = 0\n        # The document-wide reference map. Only the document root holds one.\n        self.references: ReferenceMap | None = None\n\n    def open_last_child(self) -> Block | None:\n        \"\"\"The last child if it is still open, otherwise finalize: FinalizeRule | None = None\n\n    def __post_init__(self) -> None:\n        if self.accepts_lines and self.add_line is None:\n            raise ValueError(f\"block type {self.name!r} accepts lines but has no add_line rule\")\n        if self.lazy and not self.accepts_lines:\n            raise ValueError(f\"block type {self.name!r} is lazy but does not accept lines\")\n\n\ndef _always_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    return True\n\n\ndef _paragraph_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    return not cursor.is_blank()\n\n\ndef leading link reference definitions into the document map and keep the remaining text.\n\n    A paragraph that holds only definitions leaves the tree.\n    \"\"\"\n    text = \"\\n\".join(block.lines).strip(\" \\t\")\n    block.content = extract_definitions(text, _document_references(block))\n    if not block.content and block.parent is not None:\n        block.parent.children.remove(block)\n\n\ndef _document_references(block: Block) -> ReferenceMap:\n    \"\"\"The reference map of the document root that `block` belongs to.\"\"\"\n    root = block\n    while root.parent is not None:\n        root = root.parent\n    assert root.references is not None\n    return root.references\n\n\ndef _never_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    return False\n\n\nTHEMATIC_BREAK_MARKERS = \"*-_\"\nTHEMATIC_BREAK_MIN_MARKERS = 3\n\n\ndef _thematic_break_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    \"\"\"Start a thematic break when the rest of the line is three or more matching marker characters.\n\n    Spaces and tabs may appear between and after the markers. Any other character, or four or more\n    columns of indentation, means the line is not a thematic break.\n    \"\"\"\n    if cursor.indent >= 4:\n        return None\n    start = cursor.next_nonspace()\n    line = cursor.line\n    if start == len(line) or line[start] not in THEMATIC_BREAK_MARKERS:\n        return None\n    marker = line[start]\n    count = 0\n    for char in line[start:]:\n        if char == marker:\n            count += 1\n        elif char not in SPACE_CHARS:\n            return None\n    if count < THEMATIC_BREAK_MIN_MARKERS:\n        return None\n    cursor.advance_to(len(line))\n    return Block(THEMATIC_BREAK)\n\n\nATX_MARKER = \"#\"\nATX_MAX_LEVEL = 6\n\n\ndef _atx_heading_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    \"\"\"Start an ATX heading when the line opens with one to six `#` characters.\n\n    The opening run must be followed by a space, a tab or the end of the line. So `foo#` keeps its hash, and so\n    does `foo \\\\#`, where the backslash is not whitespace.\n    \"\"\"\n    stripped = content.rstrip(ATX_MARKER)\n    if stripped == content:\n        return content\n    if stripped == \"\" or stripped[-1] in SPACE_CHARS:\n        return stripped.rstrip(SPACE_CHARS)\n    return content\n\n\nDOCUMENT = BlockType(\"document\", continues=_always_continues, is_container=True)\nPARAGRAPH = BlockType(\n    \"paragraph\",\n    continues=_paragraph_continues,\n    accepts_lines=True,\n    interruptible=True,\n    lazy=True,\n    add_line=_paragraph_add_line,\n    finalize=_paragraph_finalize,\n)\n# A thematic break is a complete single-line block. It never takes continuation lines, so it closes\n# as soon as the next line arrives.\nTHEMATIC_BREAK = BlockType(\n    \"thematic_break\",\n    continues=_never_continues,\n    start=_thematic_break_start,\n)\n\n\nclass BlockRegistry:\n    \"\"\"The block types a parse may use: the document root, the fallback paragraph, and start rules.\n\n    Start rules are tried in registration order. Match open blocks. Unmatched blocks stay open: the line may be a lazy continuation.\n        container = self._match_open_blocks(cursor)\n        all_closed = container.open_last_child() is None\n\n        # 2. Look for new block starts. Unmatched blocks are closed only once a start succeeds.\n        started = False\n        while not self._is_text_leaf(container):\n            new_block = self._try_starts(cursor, container)\n            if new_block is None:\n                break\n            if not started:\n                started = True\n                all_closed = True\n                self._close_below(container)\n            self._attach(new_block, container)\n            container = new_block\n\n        # 3. Add the remaining text to the deepest open block.\n        tip = self._tip()\n        if not all_closed and not cursor.is_blank() and tip.kind.lazy:\n            self._add_line(tip, cursor)\n Block(self.registry.fallback)\n            self._attach(paragraph, container)\n            self._add_line(paragraph, cursor)\n\n    def finish(self) -> Block:\n        \"\"\"Close every open block and return the document root.\"\"\"\n        self._close_below(self.root)\n        self.root.is_open = False\n        return self.root\n\n    def _match_open_blocks(self, cursor: Cursor) -> Block:\n        container = self.root\n        while True:\n            child = container.open_last_child()\n            if child is None or not child.kind.continues(child, cursor):\n                return container\n            container = child\n\n    def _try_starts(self, cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n        for block_type in self.registry.starts():\n            assert block_type.start is not None\n            new_block = block_type.start(cursor, container)\n            if new_block is not None:\n                return new_block\n        return None\n\n    def \"\"\"Add `new_block` under `container`, closing any leaf that cannot hold it.\"\"\"\n        while not container.kind.is_container:\n            self._finalize(container)\n            assert container.open_last_child()\n        if child is None:\n            return\n        self._close_below(child)\n        self._finalize(child)\n\n    def _finalize(self, block: Block) -> None:\n        block.is_open = False\n        if block.kind.finalize is not None:\n            block.kind.finalize(block)\n\n\ndef parse_lines(lines: Iterable[str], registry: BlockRegistry = DEFAULT_REGISTRY) -> {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01FwqfpJgdLvsq62jhvUuD2P","type":"tool_result","content":"The file /mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/CommonMark/runs/20261014.053711/build/commonmark/mdparser/blocks.py has been updated successfully."}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"215bf030-5dae-4847-abe8-edd5641cc56a","uuid":"c69608da-d456-406c-a287-039bdee9ac61","timestamp":"2026-10-14T07:08:00.127Z","tool_use_result":{"filePath":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/CommonMark/runs/20261014.053711/build/commonmark/mdparser/blocks.py","oldString":"DEFAULT_REGISTRY.register(THEMATIC_BREAK)\n","newString":"DEFAULT_REGISTRY.register(THEMATIC_BREAK)\nDEFAULT_REGISTRY.register(ATX_HEADING)\n","originalFile":"\"\"\"Phase 1: block tree, block-type registry, per-line procedure, and lazy continuation.\n\nResponsibility: consume lines one at a time, match them against open blocks, look for new block\nstarts, and add remaining text to the deepest open block. Link reference definitions are handed to\n`mdparser.refs` when a paragraph closes.\n\nEach block type is a `BlockType` record registered in a `BlockRegistry`. A type supplies a start\nrule, a continue rule and a close (finalize) rule; the per-line loop in `DocumentParser` never\nnames a concrete type.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom collections.abc import Callable, Iterable\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\nfrom mdparser.refs import ReferenceMap, extract_definitions\n\nTAB_STOP = 4\nSPACE_CHARS = \" \\t\"\n\n# A start rule inspects the rest of the line below `container`. It returns a new block, after\n# advancing the cursor past its marker, or None, leaving the cursor untouched.\nStartRule = Callable[[\"Cursor\", \"Block\"], \"Block | None\"]\n# A continue rule decides whether the line continues an open block. It advances the cursor only\n# when it returns True.\nContinueRule = Callable[[\"Block\", \"Cursor\"], bool]\n# An add-line rule appends the remaining line text to a leaf block that accepts lines.\nAddLineRule = Callable[[\"Block\", \"Cursor\"], None]\n# A finalize rule runs once when a block closes, for example to set its content.\nFinalizeRule = Callable[[\"Block\"], None]\n\n\ndef next_column(char: str, col: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the column after `char`, which sits at column `col`. Tabs advance to the next tab stop.\"\"\"\n    if char == \"\\t\":\n        return col + TAB_STOP - col % TAB_STOP\n    return col + 1\n\n\ndef indent_columns(line: str, pos: int, col: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the width in columns of the spaces and tabs starting at `pos`, which sits at `col`.\"\"\"\n    end = pos\n    end_col = col\n    while end < len(line) and line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:\n        end_col = next_column(line[end], end_col)\n        end += 1\n    return end_col - col\n\n\nclass Cursor:\n    \"\"\"A position in one source line, tracked both as a character index and as a column.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, line: str) -> None:\n        self.line = line\n        self.pos = 0\n        self.col = 0\n\n    @property\n    def rest(self) -> str:\n        \"\"\"The text from the current position to the end of the line.\"\"\"\n        return self.line[self.pos :]\n\n    @property\n    def indent(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Columns of indentation from the current position to the next non-space character.\"\"\"\n        return indent_columns(self.line, self.pos, self.col)\n\n    def next_nonspace(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Index of the first character at or after the current position that is not a space or tab.\"\"\"\n        end = self.pos\n        while end < len(self.line) and self.line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            end += 1\n        return end\n\n    def is_blank(self) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"True when only spaces and tabs remain on the line.\"\"\"\n        return self.next_nonspace() == len(self.line)\n\n    def advance_to(self, index: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Move the cursor forward to character `index`, tracking the column.\"\"\"\n        while self.pos < index:\n            self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n            self.pos += 1\n\n    def advance_nonspace(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Skip spaces and tabs up to the next non-space character.\"\"\"\n        self.advance_to(self.next_nonspace())\n\n    def advance_columns(self, columns: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Consume spaces and tabs until `columns` columns are passed.\n\n        A tab that straddles the target column is consumed whole, so the column may overshoot.\n        \"\"\"\n        target = self.col + columns\n        while self.pos < len(self.line) and self.col < target and self.line[self.pos] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n            self.pos += 1\n\n\nclass Block:\n    \"\"\"A node in the block tree. Leaf blocks keep their raw lines; `content` is set when they close.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, kind: BlockType) -> None:\n        self.kind = kind\n        self.parent: Block | None = None\n        self.children: list[Block] = []\n        self.is_open = True\n        self.lines: list[str] = []\n        self.content = \"\"\n        # Heading level, 1 to 6, for an ATX heading. Zero for every other block.\n        self.level = 0\n        # The document-wide reference map. Only the document root holds one.\n        self.references: ReferenceMap | None = None\n\n    def open_last_child(self) -> Block | None:\n        \"\"\"The last child if it is still open, otherwise None.\"\"\"\n        if self.children and self.children[-1].is_open:\n            return self.children[-1]\n        return None\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass BlockType:\n    \"\"\"The rules that define one kind of block.\n\n    `accepts_lines` marks a leaf that takes line text. `interruptible` lets a start rule close such\n    a leaf (a paragraph); a non-interruptible leaf blocks new starts. `lazy` lets a non-matching\n    line join this block as a lazy continuation. `is_container` lets the block hold child blocks.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    name: str\n    continues: ContinueRule\n    is_container: bool = False\n    accepts_lines: bool = False\n    interruptible: bool = False\n    lazy: bool = False\n    start: StartRule | None = None\n    add_line: AddLineRule | None = None\n    finalize: FinalizeRule | None = None\n\n    def __post_init__(self) -> None:\n        if self.accepts_lines and self.add_line is None:\n            raise ValueError(f\"block type {self.name!r} accepts lines but has no add_line rule\")\n        if self.lazy and not self.accepts_lines:\n            raise ValueError(f\"block type {self.name!r} is lazy but does not accept lines\")\n\n\ndef _always_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    return True\n\n\ndef _paragraph_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    return not cursor.is_blank()\n\n\ndef _paragraph_add_line(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:\n    cursor.advance_nonspace()\n    block.lines.append(cursor.rest)\n\n\ndef _paragraph_finalize(block: Block) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Move leading link reference definitions into the document map and keep the remaining text.\n\n    A paragraph that holds only definitions leaves the tree.\n    \"\"\"\n    text = \"\\n\".join(block.lines).strip(\" \\t\")\n    block.content = extract_definitions(text, _document_references(block))\n    if not block.content and block.parent is not None:\n        block.parent.children.remove(block)\n\n\ndef _document_references(block: Block) -> ReferenceMap:\n    \"\"\"The reference map of the document root that `block` belongs to.\"\"\"\n    root = block\n    while root.parent is not None:\n        root = root.parent\n    assert root.references is not None\n    return root.references\n\n\ndef _never_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    return False\n\n\nTHEMATIC_BREAK_MARKERS = \"*-_\"\nTHEMATIC_BREAK_MIN_MARKERS = 3\n\n\ndef _thematic_break_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    \"\"\"Start a thematic break when the rest of the line is three or more matching marker characters.\n\n    Spaces and tabs may appear between and after the markers. Any other character, or four or more\n    columns of indentation, means the line is not a thematic break.\n    \"\"\"\n    if cursor.indent >= 4:\n        return None\n    start = cursor.next_nonspace()\n    line = cursor.line\n    if start == len(line) or line[start] not in THEMATIC_BREAK_MARKERS:\n        return None\n    marker = line[start]\n    count = 0\n    for char in line[start:]:\n        if char == marker:\n            count += 1\n        elif char not in SPACE_CHARS:\n            return None\n    if count < THEMATIC_BREAK_MIN_MARKERS:\n        return None\n    cursor.advance_to(len(line))\n    return Block(THEMATIC_BREAK)\n\n\nATX_MARKER = \"#\"\nATX_MAX_LEVEL = 6\n\n\ndef _atx_heading_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    \"\"\"Start an ATX heading when the line opens with one to six `#` characters.\n\n    The opening run must be followed by a space, a tab or the end of the line. The content is the\n    rest of the line, stripped of surrounding spaces and tabs, without a closing sequence.\n    \"\"\"\n    if cursor.indent >= 4:\n        return None\n    line = cursor.line\n    start = cursor.next_nonspace()\n    end = start\n    while end < len(line) and line[end] == ATX_MARKER:\n        end += 1\n    level = end - start\n    if not 1 <= level <= ATX_MAX_LEVEL:\n        return None\n    if end < len(line) and line[end] not in SPACE_CHARS:\n        return None\n    cursor.advance_to(len(line))\n    heading = Block(ATX_HEADING)\n    heading.level = level\n    heading.content = _strip_closing_sequence(line[end:].strip(SPACE_CHARS))\n    return heading\n\n\ndef _strip_closing_sequence(content: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Remove a closing run of `#` characters from the end of heading content.\n\n    The run must be the whole content or follow a space or tab. So `foo#` keeps its hash, and so\n    does `foo \\\\#`, where the backslash is not whitespace.\n    \"\"\"\n    stripped = content.rstrip(ATX_MARKER)\n    if stripped == content:\n        return content\n    if stripped == \"\" or stripped[-1] in SPACE_CHARS:\n        return stripped.rstrip(SPACE_CHARS)\n    return content\n\n\nDOCUMENT = BlockType(\"document\", continues=_always_continues, is_container=True)\nPARAGRAPH = BlockType(\n    \"paragraph\",\n    continues=_paragraph_continues,\n    accepts_lines=True,\n    interruptible=True,\n    lazy=True,\n    add_line=_paragraph_add_line,\n    finalize=_paragraph_finalize,\n)\n# A thematic break is a complete single-line block. It never takes continuation lines, so it closes\n# as soon as the next line arrives.\nTHEMATIC_BREAK = BlockType(\n    \"thematic_break\",\n    continues=_never_continues,\n    start=_thematic_break_start,\n)\n# An ATX heading is a complete single-line block, like a thematic break. Its content is parsed as\n# inlines when the document is rendered.\nATX_HEADING = BlockType(\n    \"atx_heading\",\n    continues=_never_continues,\n    start=_atx_heading_start,\n)\n\n\nclass BlockRegistry:\n    \"\"\"The block types a parse may use: the document root, the fallback paragraph, and start rules.\n\n    Start rules are tried in registration order. The fallback type is the paragraph created when no\n    start rule matches a line of text.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, root: BlockType, fallback: BlockType) -> None:\n        self.root = root\n        self.fallback = fallback\n        self._names: set[str] = set()\n        self._starts: list[BlockType] = []\n        self.register(root)\n        self.register(fallback)\n\n    def register(self, block_type: BlockType) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Add a block type. Its start rule, if any, joins the start rules in order.\"\"\"\n        if block_type.name in self._names:\n            raise ValueError(f\"block type already registered: {block_type.name!r}\")\n        self._names.add(block_type.name)\n        if block_type.start is not None:\n            self._starts.append(block_type)\n\n    def starts(self) -> tuple[BlockType, ...]:\n        \"\"\"The registered block types that have a start rule, in registration order.\"\"\"\n        return tuple(self._starts)\n\n\nDEFAULT_REGISTRY = BlockRegistry(root=DOCUMENT, fallback=PARAGRAPH)\nDEFAULT_REGISTRY.register(THEMATIC_BREAK)\n\n\nclass DocumentParser:\n    \"\"\"Runs the phase 1 per-line procedure over a document, one line at a time.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, registry: BlockRegistry = DEFAULT_REGISTRY) -> None:\n        self.registry = registry\n        self.root = Block(registry.root)\n        self.root.references = ReferenceMap()\n\n    def incorporate_line(self, line: str) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Match open blocks, look for new starts, then add the remaining text.\"\"\"\n        cursor = Cursor(line)\n\n        # 1. Match open blocks. Unmatched blocks stay open: the line may be a lazy continuation.\n        container = self._match_open_blocks(cursor)\n        all_closed = container.open_last_child() is None\n\n        # 2. Look for new block starts. Unmatched blocks are closed only once a start succeeds.\n        started = False\n        while not self._is_text_leaf(container):\n            new_block = self._try_starts(cursor, container)\n            if new_block is None:\n                break\n            if not started:\n                started = True\n                all_closed = True\n                self._close_below(container)\n            self._attach(new_block, container)\n            container = new_block\n\n        # 3. Add the remaining text to the deepest open block.\n        tip = self._tip()\n        if not all_closed and not cursor.is_blank() and tip.kind.lazy:\n            self._add_line(tip, cursor)\n            return\n        self._close_below(container)\n        if container.kind.accepts_lines:\n            self._add_line(container, cursor)\n        elif not cursor.is_blank():\n            paragraph = Block(self.registry.fallback)\n            self._attach(paragraph, container)\n            self._add_line(paragraph, cursor)\n\n    def finish(self) -> Block:\n        \"\"\"Close every open block and return the document root.\"\"\"\n        self._close_below(self.root)\n        self.root.is_open = False\n        return self.root\n\n    def _match_open_blocks(self, cursor: Cursor) -> Block:\n        container = self.root\n        while True:\n            child = container.open_last_child()\n            if child is None or not child.kind.continues(child, cursor):\n                return container\n            container = child\n\n    def _try_starts(self, cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n        for block_type in self.registry.starts():\n            assert block_type.start is not None\n            new_block = block_type.start(cursor, container)\n            if new_block is not None:\n                return new_block\n        return None\n\n    def _is_text_leaf(self, block: Block) -> bool:\n        return block.kind.accepts_lines and not block.kind.interruptible\n\n    def _attach(self, new_block: Block, container: Block) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Add `new_block` under `container`, closing any leaf that cannot hold it.\"\"\"\n        while not container.kind.is_container:\n            self._finalize(container)\n            assert container.parent is not None\n            container = container.parent\n        container.children.append(new_block)\n        new_block.parent = container\n\n    def _add_line(self, block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:\n        assert block.kind.add_line is not None\n        block.kind.add_line(block, cursor)\n\n    def _tip(self) -> Block:\n        \"\"\"The deepest open block.\"\"\"\n        tip = self.root\n        while (child := tip.open_last_child()) is not None:\n            tip = child\n        return tip\n\n    def _close_below(self, container: Block) -> None:\n        child = container.open_last_child()\n        if child is None:\n            return\n        self._close_below(child)\n        self._finalize(child)\n\n    def _finalize(self, block: Block) -> None:\n        block.is_open = False\n        if block.kind.finalize is not None:\n            block.kind.finalize(block)\n\n\ndef parse_lines(lines: Iterable[str], registry: BlockRegistry = DEFAULT_REGISTRY) -> Block:\n    \"\"\"Build the block tree for `lines`, which hold no line-ending characters.\"\"\"\n    parser = DocumentParser(registry)\n    for line in lines:\n        parser.incorporate_line(line)\n    return parser.finish()\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":311,"oldLines":6,"newStart":311,"newLines":7,"lines":[" "," DEFAULT_REGISTRY = BlockRegistry(root=DOCUMENT, fallback=PARAGRAPH)"," {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_014KBRZ1QhdeFiCAWtZ5Kn5r","type":"tool_result","content":"The file /mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/CommonMark/runs/20261014.053711/build/commonmark/mdparser/render.py has been updated successfully."}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"215bf030-5dae-4847-abe8-edd5641cc56a","uuid":"1f63be0f-03ed-4e56-bdf0-45f0fd043377","timestamp":"2026-10-14T07:08:01.233Z","tool_use_result":{"filePath":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/CommonMark/runs/20261014.053711/build/commonmark/mdparser/render.py","oldString":"    if block.kind.name == \"thematic_break\":\n        return \"<hr />\\n\"\n    raise","newString":"    if block.kind.name == \"thematic_break\":\n        return \"<hr />\\n\"\n    if block.kind.name == \"atx_heading\":\n        return f\"<h{block.level}>{parse_inline(block.content)}</h{block.level}>\\n\"\n    raise","originalFile":"\"\"\"HTML rendering.\n\nResponsibility: turn the parsed tree into HTML, escape HTML text and attributes, and\npercent-encode URLs. The conformance runner compares normalized HTML, so tag structure and\nentities must match the spec examples.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport string\nfrom collections.abc import Callable\n\nfrom mdparser.blocks import Block\n\nInlineParser = Callable[[str], str]\n\nESCAPES = ((\"&\", \"&amp;\"), (\"<\", \"&lt;\"), (\">\", \"&gt;\"), ('\"', \"&quot;\"))\nURL_SAFE_CHARS = frozenset(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + \";,/?:@&=+$-_.!~*'()#\")\nHEX_DIGITS = frozenset(string.hexdigits)\n\n\ndef escape_html(text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Escape &, <, > and \" so the text renders as literal characters. The ampersand goes first.\"\"\"\n    for raw, entity in ESCAPES:\n        text = text.replace(raw, entity)\n    return text\n\n\ndef percent_encode_url(url: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Percent-encode a URL for use in an attribute.\n\n    URL-safe ASCII and existing %XX escapes are kept. Every other character is encoded as its\n    UTF-8 bytes, so a lone % becomes %25.\n    \"\"\"\n    out: list[str] = []\n    index = 0\n    while index < len(url):\n        char = url[index]\n        if char == \"%\" and _is_hex_pair(url[index + 1 : index + 3]):\n            out.append(url[index : index + 3])\n            index += 3\n            continue\n        if char in URL_SAFE_CHARS:\n            out.append(char)\n        else:\n            out.extend(f\"%{byte:02X}\" for byte in char.encode(\"utf-8\"))\n        index += 1\n    return \"\".join(out)\n\n\ndef _is_hex_pair(text: str) -> bool:\n    return len(text) == 2 and all(char in HEX_DIGITS for char in text)\n\n\ndef render_document(root: Block, parse_inline: InlineParser) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Phase 2 walk: render the top-level blocks in order, one line ending after each block.\n\n    `parse_inline` is the inline parser hook. It receives the raw content of each paragraph and\n    returns that content's HTML.\n    \"\"\"\n    return \"\".join(_render_block(child, parse_inline) for child in root.children)\n\n\ndef _render_block(block: Block, parse_inline: InlineParser) -> str:\n    if block.kind.name == \"paragraph\":\n        return f\"<p>{parse_inline(block.content)}</p>\\n\"\n    if block.kind.name == \"thematic_break\":\n        return \"<hr />\\n\"\n    raise ValueError(f\"no HTML renderer for block type {block.kind.name!r}\")\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":66,"oldLines":4,"newStart":66,"newLines":6,"lines":["         return f\"<p>{parse_inline(block.content)}</p>\\n\"","     if block.kind.name == \"thematic_break\":","         return \"<hr />\\n\"","+    if block.kind.name == \"atx_heading\":","+        return f\"<h{block.level}>{parse_inline(block.content)}</h{block.level}>\\n\"","     raise ValueError(f\"no HTML renderer for block type {block.kind.name!r}\")"]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false,"contentNotInModelContext":true},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_014KBRZ1QhdeFiCAWtZ5Kn5r","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}
